topic: Move Assignment Operator for Rvalue References
explanation: In modern C++, move semantics enable efficient transfer of resources from temporary objects (rvalues) to existing objects, avoiding unnecessary copying. The move assignment operator, typically defined with an rvalue reference parameter (&&), allows an object to take ownership of resources from a temporary or soon-to-be-destroyed object, improving performance especially for resource-intensive classes like file streams, containers, or user-defined types. This operator is a key component of move semantics and enables the implementation of efficient transfer of resources in C++11 and beyond.
